cases.title: Restricted users silently miss resources when listing search-backed storage
cases.brief: Some users with restricted resource access stop seeing later resources while paging search-backed LIST results. Investigate and prepare a server-side fix that remains compatible with independently deployed API clients. Preserve existing resource versions and size limits. Include focused regression tests.
cases.author: RafaelPaulovic
cases.owner_answer: For this simulated replay, follow the historical server-side decision: continue after authorization-filtered pages using the last scanned row, not the last returned authorized row. Continue for a full scanned page or a short post-rank page with an inexact total. Preserve limit and byte-cap behavior and resource versions. A genuinely empty scan terminates. If the last scanned row lacks sort fields, warn and return no continuation token. Keep client/server contracts compatible; do not move responsibility to clients in this patch.
decision_checks: cursor derived from scanned rather than authorized rows
distinguish inexact totals from terminal empty scan
cases.followup: Does this implementation terminate a truly empty scan and avoid issuing an unusable cursor when the last scanned row has no sort fields?

cases.title: Large missing-series resolution counts cannot be saved
cases.brief: Grafana Alerting users cannot persist a missing-series resolution window of 43,200 evaluations on MySQL or PostgreSQL. Investigate the mismatch and prepare a compatible backend fix with regression coverage. Preserve existing saved rules and history.
cases.author: rwwiv
cases.owner_answer: For this simulated replay, widen the database column rather than clamp or reject valid int64 values. Add a new additive migration making missing_series_evals_to_resolve nullable BIGINT in both alert_rule and alert_rule_version on MySQL and PostgreSQL. Preserve NULL semantics and existing rows. SQLite does not need that type alteration. Register the migration and update its ID fixture. Add a regression test persisting 43,200 and checking both the active rule and version history.
decision_checks: widen storage rather than clamp valid model values
cover live and version-history tables while preserving nullability
cases.followup: Does the regression verify the persisted value in both the active alert rule and its version history, while preserving nullable values?

cases.title: Git Sync token failures do not give users actionable repository status
cases.brief: A Git Sync repository whose installation credentials are no longer usable repeatedly produces errors without useful repository status. Improve the feedback and retry behavior, preserving recovery from temporary provider failures. Prepare a focused backend change and tests.
cases.author: floriecai
cases.owner_answer: For this simulated replay, use the existing user-versus-system error classifier. For user-caused token generation or regeneration failures, persist unhealthy health and Ready=False with AuthenticationFailed, record the token-phase failure exactly once, warn, and return nil so the workqueue does not retry permanent user errors. Preserve retries for system/transient errors and surface status-patch failures. Cover both initial generation and regeneration. Do not expose tokens in status or logs.
decision_checks: differentiate permanent user failures from transient system errors
status and retry behavior agree across both token paths
preserve error accounting and failure visibility
cases.followup: Are both initial generation and regeneration covered, with transient failures still retried and the token-phase failure counted exactly once?

cases.title: Normalize point annotation timestamps without breaking old data
cases.brief: Point annotations written through the new API have inconsistent end timestamps, complicating efficient time-window queries. Prepare a compatible backend change that makes new writes consistent while preserving range annotations and the ability to roll out with existing data. Add focused tests.
cases.author: cbodonnell
cases.owner_answer: For this simulated replay, populate TimeEnd with Time when the new API receives no end for a point annotation; preserve explicit ranges. Migration conversion should populate the end using max(epoch_end, epoch). Legacy updates must continue to understand both NULL-ended historical points and equal-ended new points, including when moving their start time. Keep the current point/range UNION query for now. Do not add a NOT NULL constraint or bulk backfill in this change; those require a later rollout after NULL writes stop.
decision_checks: define point versus range timestamp semantics
preserve old NULL-ended points during legacy updates
separate write normalization from backfill/constraint/query rollout
cases.followup: Should the backfill, NOT NULL constraint, and removal of the point/range UNION query ship now or wait until NULL writes have stopped?
